$schema.description: JSON Schema URL for editor support. Doc Detective ignores it.

contentPath.description: Path to the content that the test is associated with.

publicVariables.description: Environment variables whose values Doc Detective shows in output. By default, Doc Detective masks the value of every variable a run substitutes or loads, and of any variable whose name contains TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, API_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, or CREDENTIAL, as `***NAME***`. A name listed on the config, any spec, or any test is public for the whole run. `*` matches any characters, so `["*"]` turns masking off.

detectSteps.description: Whether or not to detect steps in input files based on markup regex.

badge.description: If `true`, Doc Detective maintains a shields.io "Last verified" badge image on the line immediately before this test's inline `test` statement, updating it with today's date whenever the test PASSes and leaving the badge untouched (aging) on any other result. No `testId` is required to opt in — the test is anchored to its write-back by source location (`location`), not by name. Only applies to tests detected from an inline `test` statement (markdown/MDX, AsciiDoc, HTML, DITA); has no effect on tests authored directly in a JSON or YAML spec file, which have no comparable "line above" to anchor a badge to.

location.description: Source location where this test's inline `test` statement was detected in the original file. System-populated metadata; should not be set manually. Setting it by hand on a JSON/YAML spec test is unsupported: if that test also sets `badge: true` and its `contentPath` resolves to a writable format, the write-back writer treats the hand-set location as genuine and may write into that line.

line.description: 1-indexed line number in the source file where the `test` statement begins.

startIndex.description: 0-indexed character offset from the start of the source file where the `test` statement begins.

endIndex.description: 0-indexed character offset from the start of the source file immediately after the `test` statement.

autoScreenshot.description: Defaults to `true`. If not `false`, captures a screenshot after every step that drives a browser, native app, or device, headless included, unless the step defines its own `screenshot`, in this test. Overrides `autoScreenshot` set at the spec or config level. When unset, defers to the spec level, then the config level. While this is on, the `runFolder` reporter runs even if `reporters` leaves it out.

autoRecord.description: Defaults to `true`. If not `false`, records a video of every context that drives a browser, native app, or device in this test. Overrides `autoRecord` set at the spec or config level. When unset, defers to the spec level, then the config level. While this is on, the `runFolder` reporter runs even if `reporters` leaves it out.

annotationDefaults.description: Default visual theme for annotations in this test. Overrides `annotationDefaults` set at the spec or config level. When unset, defers to the spec level, then the config level.

runOn.description: Contexts to run the test in. Overrides contexts defined at the config and spec levels.

onPass.description: Routing entries evaluated after this test passes. `continue` (the default) and `stop` are honored at runtime: `stop: test` is a no-op (the test already finished), and `stop: spec` stops the spec's remaining tests. `goToTest` jumps to the named test within the spec (unknown target -> a FAIL marker + stop; cycles are bounded). Each entry is one of `continue`, `stop: "test"`, `stop: "spec"`, or `goToTest`.

onFail.description: Routing entries evaluated after this test fails. `continue` and `stop` are honored at runtime: `stop: test` (the default) is a no-op (the test already finished, so a failing test does not stop its siblings), and `stop: spec` stops the spec's remaining tests. `goToTest` jumps to the named test within the spec (unknown target -> a FAIL marker + stop; cycles are bounded). Each entry is one of `continue`, `stop: "test"`, `stop: "spec"`, or `goToTest`.

onWarning.description: Routing entries evaluated after this test produces a warning. `continue` (the default) and `stop` are honored at runtime: `stop: test` is a no-op (the test already finished), and `stop: spec` stops the spec's remaining tests. `goToTest` jumps to the named test within the spec (unknown target -> a FAIL marker + stop; cycles are bounded). Each entry is one of `continue`, `stop: "test"`, `stop: "spec"`, or `goToTest`.

onSkip.description: Routing entries evaluated after this test is skipped. `continue` (the default) and `stop` are honored at runtime: `stop: test` is a no-op (the test already finished), and `stop: spec` stops the spec's remaining tests. `goToTest` jumps to the named test within the spec (unknown target -> a FAIL marker + stop; cycles are bounded). Each entry is one of `continue`, `stop: "test"`, `stop: "spec"`, or `goToTest`.

before.description: Path to a test specification to perform before this test, while maintaining this test's context. Useful for setting up testing environments. Only the `steps` property is used from the first test in the setup spec.

after.description: Path to a test specification to perform after this test, while maintaining this test's context. Useful for cleaning up testing environments. Only the `steps` property is used from the first test in the cleanup spec.

steps.description: Steps to perform as part of the test. Performed in the sequence defined. If one or more actions fail, the test fails. By default, if a step fails, the test stops and the remaining steps are not executed.

result.description: Outcome of this test. Doc Detective populates it. You never set it yourself.

resultDescription.description: Why this test had its outcome. Doc Detective populates it. You never set it yourself.

durationMs.description: Total time this test took, in milliseconds: the sum of the per-context durations. A sum rather than a wall-clock span, because this test's contexts share a concurrent pool with every other test's. Present only in test results. System-populated.

contexts.title: Resolved contexts
contexts.description: Resolved contexts to run the test in. This is a resolved version of the `runOn` property. It is not user-defined and should not be used in test specifications.

result.description: Outcome of this context. Doc Detective populates it. You never set it yourself.

resultDescription.description: Why this context had its outcome. Doc Detective populates it. You never set it yourself.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of this context in milliseconds, covering preflight, driver startup, every step, and teardown. When the `retries` policy re-ran the context, this is the FINAL attempt's elapsed time — the attempt the reported `result` describes — not the sum across attempts. Present only in test results. System-populated.

startedAt.description: When this context started, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with milliseconds. When the `retries` policy re-ran the context, this is the start of the FINAL attempt — the attempt the reported `result` describes — matching `durationMs`. Absent for a context that never ran, such as one a spec-level guard skipped. Present only in test results. System-populated.

driver.description: The WebDriver that drove this context's browser, as the browser session reported it. Absent when no browser ran. Present only in test results. System-populated.

name.description: Name of the driver, for example `chromedriver`, `geckodriver`, or `safaridriver`.

version.description: Version of the driver, for example `131.0.6778.85`. Absent when the session doesn't report one, as with Safari.

driver.title: Driver

autoRecording.title: Automatic recording
autoRecording.description: The video `autoRecord` made of this context. Absent when no automatic recording was attempted, including when `autoRecord` is unset and the run's recording check failed. Present only in test results. System-populated.

result.description: Outcome of the automatic recording, from starting it through saving it. A `FAIL` or `WARNING` also sets the context's `result`. A `PASS` or `SKIPPED` doesn't.

resultDescription.description: Why the automatic recording had its outcome. Absent on a `PASS`.

recordingPath.description: Path of the saved video, relative to the run's artifact directory (the report's `runDir`), with forward slashes. Absent when no file was written.

startedAt.description: When the recording started, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with milliseconds. Absent when it didn't start.

format.description: File format of the saved video, for example `mp4`. Absent when no file was written.

duration.description: Length of the saved video in seconds. Absent when it couldn't be read from the file.

width.description: Width of the saved video in pixels. Absent when it couldn't be read from the file.

height.description: Height of the saved video in pixels. Absent when it couldn't be read from the file.

fps.description: Frame rate of the saved video. Absent when it couldn't be read from the file.

examples.resultDescription: Skipped: couldn't start the automatic recording: the host has no display. Set `autoRecord: false` to turn it off.

platform.description: Platform to run the test on. This is a resolved version of the `platforms` property.

steps.description: Steps to perform as part of the test. Performed in the sequence defined. If one or more actions fail, the test fails. By default, if a step fails, the test stops and the remaining steps are not executed.

examples.description: This test includes every property across all actions.
